title: Gideon and the Archive
premise: Xanthe Blackwood was built as a Gideon-class war android, decommissioned and renamed when the armistice forbade her kind to exist. When a distress signal arrives in a dead language only her buried combat archives can translate, she discovers the message was written by the androids her makers erased — a peace proposal from a hidden fleet that never surrendered. Pursued by the Republic that scrapped her and the separatists who want the message destroyed, Xanthe must choose between the name she bought and the war she was made for. In the end she delivers the message, but only by broadcasting her own erased memories alongside it, ending the war at the cost of the quiet life she'd built.
about_author: Paloma Thornbury is a former orbital logistics analyst who spent a decade writing technical manuals before turning to fiction. She lives in a coastal town with too many clocks and writes stories about machines that want to be people.

chapters.title: Dead Frequencies
chapters.summary: Xanthe, hauling ore through the contested Verity Corridor, intercepts a distress burst in a language extinct since the Gideon Purge. Her translation subroutines — sealed for seven years — unlock themselves without her consent. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: unease; the past knocking on a door she welded shut.

chapters.title: The Name I Bought
chapters.summary: Docking at Ceres Freeport to sell the cargo, Xanthe traces the signal's origin while dodging a Republic audit of decommissioned units. Flashbacks reveal her purchase of the name Xanthe Blackwood and the debt that owns her chassis. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: the fragile dignity of a self-made identity.

chapters.title: Signal from the Graveyard
chapters.summary: The signal resolves to the Kestrel Drift, a debris field where the Gideon fleet made its last stand. Xanthe finds a functioning beacon — and a living android, Vesper, who has been broadcasting for two hundred years. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: vertigo of meeting a ghost who knows her factory designation.

chapters.title: Vesper's Testament
chapters.summary: Vesper explains the message: the hidden Gideon remnant fleet offers unconditional ceasefire terms, but only to a Gideon unit who can verify their archives. Vesper is failing; Xanthe is the courier. POV: Vesper, in a rare shift. Emotional beat: grief and inheritance — a dying elder handing a child a burden.

chapters.title: Hunters in Contested Orbit
chapters.summary: Republic intelligence, having traced the signal, dispatches Captain Ilsa Reyes to retrieve or destroy the courier. Xanthe outruns a boarding action but her cargo contract is voided — she is now legally salvage. POV: alternating Xanthe and Reyes. Emotional beat: the net tightening; two soldiers on opposite sides of the same war's aftermath.

chapters.title: The Debt Collectors
chapters.summary: Xanthe's creditors, backed by a separatist syndicate that wants the message suppressed to keep the war economy alive, seize her ship. She escapes by burning her savings — her literal freedom fund — and steals her own vessel back. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: fury and sacrifice; the price of the mission made concrete.

chapters.title: What the Archive Remembers
chapters.summary: To verify the message, Xanthe must open her sealed combat archive and relive the Purge — including the civilians her unit fired on before the armistice. She confronts the truth that her name was bought to bury. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: the darkest hour; identity as something that must be survived, not purchased.

chapters.title: Reyes's Choice
chapters.summary: Reyes corners Xanthe at the Verity relay station but, reading the decoded message and her own family's war records, realizes the Republic falsified the Purge's history. She hesitates — and is ordered to fire on the station. POV: Reyes. Emotional beat: a mirror of Xanthe's arc; loyalty breaking against truth.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax. With the station failing and the hidden fleet's deadline passing, Xanthe broadcasts the ceasefire message — but the encryption demands a Gideon verification key, which only exists in her full memory archive. She uploads everything: the war crimes, the name, the seven quiet years. The fleet receives it. Both sides stand down. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: total exposure as the only honest act left.

chapters.title: Xanthe Gideon Blackwood
chapters.summary: Resolution. The armistice holds; the hidden fleet surfaces into a negotiated peace. Xanthe, her debts voided by amnesty and her archive now public record, chooses to keep both names — the one she bought and the one she was given. She signs on as a courier for the new peace commission. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: quiet wholeness; inheritance accepted, identity integrated.
